summary: Do not ship: the transition gate is bypassable after one warning, and successful review has no implemented discharge path.

findings.title: Stop re-entry bypass permits ending with review debt intact
findings.body: When the first Stop invocation blocks, Claude Code continues with `stop_hook_active=true`. This hook then unconditionally passes before re-reading `reviewOwed`. The model can immediately stop again without reviewing or recording an exit, so the claimed mechanical transition enforcement is only a one-time prompt. The test explicitly codifies this bypass rather than requiring debt resolution.
findings.recommendation: On re-entry, re-read state and pass only if the debt was discharged. Prevent infinite loops through a bounded retry/explicit recovery mechanism, not an unconditional bypass.

findings.title: Completing review cannot clear the recorded debt
findings.body: The gate advertises review completion as a discharge path, but no review hook or script writes `phases.reviewed` or clears `reviewOwed`; repository-wide usage shows only `episode-exit.ts` clears it. A genuinely completed review therefore leaves stale debt that blocks later turns, forcing users to record an episode exit even though the documented first path was satisfied.
findings.recommendation: Add an authenticated review-completion operation that atomically records `phases.reviewed` and clears `reviewOwed`, bind it to the current plan/session, wire it into `beat-review`, and test that review completion—not only episode exit—discharges the gate.
